text.p: Valley National Gases Inc could add $20 million in sales in fiscal 1998 via acquisitions and will generate internal growth as well by improving operating efficiencies and market share, President and Chief Executive Officer Larry Bandi said.

"Our strategy is growth through acquisitions in new and existing markets," Bandi, 43, told Reuters in an interview. "But we're not just an acquisitions company...we're going to continue an internally-generated growth.
"Our internal rate of growth has been, and exceeds, gross domestic product growth consistently over the years we've been in business...so we do better than the normal (national) growth."
Valley National Gases, headquartered in Wheeling, W.Va., was founded in 1958 and went public last April with an initial offering of two million shares.
The company is a packager and distributor of industrial, medical and specialty gases and propane, as well as welding equipment and supplies, in 10 states in the Middle Atlantic and Midwest.
The company has historically grown through acquiring other distributors, buying about 42 independent distributors since the early 1970s.
Bandi said that strategy will continue and the company could do a market offering of an additional one million shares.

"(Acquiring other companies) is an ongoing process. I don't see a start and a stop to it," he said. "We've been doing it since 1958...there are still 1,000 distributors available in the welding supply, industrial gas and propane business."
The company's most recent acquisition was last month, when it bought Doansco Inc, an industrial gas and welding supply distributor in Hamilton, Ohio, with annualized sales of about $2 million.
"We have about 20 candidates in the pipeline today," Bandi said. "I think (adding $20 million a year in sales through acquisitions) is certainly obtainable and realistic."
Bandi said acquisition opportunities are plentiful in the distributor business because of a spate of aging executives who are near retirement and have no heirs to their businesses.

"We've had a significant consolidation in our industry," he said. "Most of the businesses in our industry were started after (World War II) and the owners are reaching retirement age and want to get out."

Besides growing through acquisitions, Bandi said the company will generate internal growth by increasing same-store sales and growing market share. "We leverage our distribution system with new products to the same customer," he said. "We look to see what we can supply that customer that they're buying elsewhere...we'll also improve margins through increasing operational efficiencies."
Separately, Bandi said he was comfortable with analysts' estimates of $0.09 per share for the fiscal first quarter and $0.46 per share for fiscal 1998.
The first quarter ends September 30. Fiscal '98 closes June 30.
Earnings in fiscal '97 were $0.33 per share before special noncash charges. Sales were $73.9 million, an increase of 37.9 percent from the prior year.
